items.stem:
In this question k is a real parameter.
(a) For f_k(x) = 2(x − k)² + k, find the vertex of the graph in terms of k.
(b) Show that the vertices of all graphs in the family lie on a straight line and state its equation.
(c) Find the values of k for which f_k(x) = 0 has two distinct real roots.
(d) Find the value of k for which the graph passes through the origin, other than k = 0.
(e) Generalise: for g_k(x) = (x − k)² + mk, find the locus of the vertex and the values of k giving real roots.
(f) Comment on how the family changes as k increases.
items.answer: (a) (k, k) (b) y = x (c) k < 0 (d) −1/2 (e) y = mx; real roots when mk ≤ 0 (f) congruent parabolas translated along the line of vertices

An inequality such as ax² + bx + c > 0, solved by finding the roots and using the shape of the parabola

items.stem: Explain how the sign of a determines the shape of y = ax² + bx + c.
items.answer: For large |x| the ax² term dominates: if a > 0 then y → +∞ and the parabola opens upwards (minimum vertex); if a < 0 it opens downwards (maximum).

items.stem: Briefly explain why completing the square gives the vertex directly.
items.answer: In a(x − h)² + k the squared term is 0 only at x = h and otherwise has the sign of a, so k is the minimum (a > 0) or maximum (a < 0) value, attained at x = h.

items.stem: Briefly explain why the discriminant tells you the number of x-intercepts of y = ax² + bx + c.
items.answer: The x-intercepts are the real roots; in the quadratic formula √Δ is real and non-zero, zero, or not real according as Δ > 0, = 0, < 0, giving 2, 1 or 0 roots.

items.stem: A student claims: "kx² + 6x + k = 0 has real roots when 36 − 4k² > 0, so −3 < k < 3." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Real roots need Δ ≥ 0: −3 ≤ k ≤ 3 (and for k = 0 the equation is linear with one root).
items.markingKey: Real roots need Δ ≥ 0: −3 ≤ k ≤ 3 (and for k = 0 the equation is linear with one root). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Let f(x) = (x + 3)(x − 1). Write f(x) in the form ax² + bx + c and in the form a(x − h)² + k, and state the equation of the axis of symmetry.
items.markingKey: expand (A1); axis at midpoint of roots x = −1 (M1 A1); k = f(−1) = −4 (A1).

items.stem: A student claims: "x² − 6x + 9 = 0 has no solution because Δ = 0." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Δ = 0 means one repeated real root, x = 3.

items.stem:
This question investigates a family of quadratic functions.
(a) For f_k(x) = 3(x − k)² + k, find the vertex of the graph in terms of k.
(b) Show that the vertices of all graphs in the family lie on a straight line and state its equation.
(c) Find the values of k for which f_k(x) = 0 has two distinct real roots.
(d) Find the value of k for which the graph passes through the origin, other than k = 0.
(e) Generalise: for g_k(x) = (x − k)² + mk, find the locus of the vertex and the values of k giving real roots.
items.answer: (a) (k, k) (b) y = x (c) k < 0 (d) −1/3 (e) y = mx; real roots when mk ≤ 0
